stem:
Charu's scooter has a convex side-view mirror. Shopkeepers also use convex mirrors for surveillance, and some roads use them at sharp bends.

Charu asks why a convex mirror is chosen for these uses.

options.text: A convex mirror forms erect, smaller images and shows a larger view area than a plane mirror.
A convex mirror forms inverted, magnified images like a microscope.
A convex mirror is chosen only because its frame is curved, not because of the image it forms.
A convex side-view mirror shows less of the traffic behind than a plane mirror would.

parts.text: Give one reason for your choice.

part_answers.answer: Erect, diminished images with a wide field of view help show more of the surroundings behind or around the observer.

teacher.key_rationale: Convex mirrors give erect, smaller images and a larger view area, which suits side-view, bend, and surveillance uses.
